deity.en: The Devi as Biraja (Girija), a form of Durga

bodyPart.en: Navel (as given in later tables; the Ashtadasha Stotram itself names no body part)

history.en: The Biraja temple stands in Jajpur, about 125 km north of Bhubaneswar in Odisha, and gave the town its nicknames Biraja Kshetra and Biraja Pitha. The Pithanirnaya's 'Viraja-kshetra in Utkala' leads some traditions to identify Biraja with the Utkala pitha of the 51, which is usually placed at Puri's Vimala temple.

story.en: According to the Puranas, Sati, the daughter of Daksha, gave up her life in the fire of her father's sacrifice after he insulted her husband Shiva. Grieving, Shiva carried her body across the world until Vishnu's discus divided it, and each place where a part fell became a Shakti Peetha. Tradition holds that Sati's navel fell here. Adi Shankara's Ashtadasha Shakti Peetha Stotram praises the goddess here as 'Odhyane Girija Devi'.

en: The two-armed Durga spears the chest of Mahishasura, shown as a water buffalo, with one hand and pulls his tail with the other.
One of her feet rests on a lion and the other on Mahishasura's chest.
Jajpur is believed to hold about one crore Shiva lingas.

timings.en: No official timings are published; check locally before visiting.

nearestAirport.en: Bhubaneswar (Biju Patnaik International Airport), about 125 km away.
